title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: declarative agents with actions in GCC High and DoD
summary: The briefing accurately reports the roadmap and Microsoft's conflicting government-cloud documentation. Its control paths, licensing statements and API limitations are supported, and the remaining uncertainties are appropriately identified.

claims.where: front matter: status; summary; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists the feature as Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched"

claims.where: front matter: releasePhase; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; title; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists GCC High and DoD, and no other clouds, for this item.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["GCC High", "DoD"]

claims.claim: The roadmap platforms are Desktop and Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Desktop", "Web"]

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap target date is June CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "June CY2026"

claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: The roadmap describes actions as invoking APIs, plugins and enterprise workflows within the Copilot chat experience.
claims.quote: Declarative Agents with Actions enable Microsoft 365 Copilot to take real-world actions by invoking APIs, plugins, and enterprise workflows directly within the chat experience.

claims.claim: The roadmap says actions are powered through API plugins, MCP tools and enterprise connectors.
claims.quote: These actions are powered through API plugins, MCP tools, and enterprise connectors

claims.claim: The roadmap says Copilot selects an appropriate action for the user's intent.
claims.quote: The Copilot platform dynamically reasons over available actions and selects the appropriate tool to fulfill user intent

claims.claim: Learn describes MCP and API plugins as custom actions for declarative agents.
claims.quote: MCP and API plugins are custom actions that enable declarative agents in Microsoft 365 Copilot to interact with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers or REST APIs

claims.claim: Copilot reads a plugin manifest to learn about the API or MCP server.
claims.quote: An API or MCP plugin uses a plugin manifest that Copilot reads to learn about the API or MCP server available to the agent.

claims.claim: Copilot decides when the agent should use the integration.
claims.quote: Copilot can then decide when the agent should use that integration to answer a prompt.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Copilot asks the user to allow or cancel the first use of an MCP or API plugin.
claims.quote: The first time Microsoft 365 Copilot uses a Model Context Protocol (MCP) or API plugin, it notifies the user and asks them to allow or cancel the operation.

claims.claim: After the initial connection confirmation, data-retrieving operations do not prompt by default.
claims.quote: After the user confirms the connection, MCP server tools and APIs that only retrieve data don't require confirmation

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Operations that modify data prompt for confirmation by default.
claims.quote: tools and APIs that modify data do. Plugin developers can override these defaults.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Developers can override confirmation for an API operation using x-openai-isConsequential in its OpenAPI document.
claims.quote: Setting this property to `false` disables the confirmation prompt, and setting it to `true` enables it.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Developers can override confirmation for an MCP tool through readOnlyHint in the tools/list response.
claims.quote: for a specific tool by setting the `readOnlyHint` property to `true` for the tool in the MCP server's `tools/list` response.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The plugin's API or MCP server is hosted outside Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: The agent sends a request to the plugin's MCP server or API, which is hosted outside of Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Copilot maps parts of the user's question to function parameters and sends a request to the plugin.
claims.quote: It maps parts of the user's question to the parameters of the function: `budgetName=""`.

claims.quote: Agent Builder is also now available in GCCH.

claims.claim: The overview says DoD supports only pro-code agents built with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit.

claims.claim: The overview says Agent Builder is not available for declarative agents in DoD.
claims.quote: Agent Builder isn't available for declarative agents in DoD.

claims.claim: The service description restricts GCC-High support to Agent Builder declarative agents and those published via admin controls.

claims.quote: Searched: declarative agents actions GCC High DoD identity authentication user signed in. Read plugin-authentication and known-issues: general signed-in-user authentication is documented, but authenticated custom actions are unsupported in Government; no cloud-specific execution identity stated.

claims.claim: The Agents Toolkit route requires an administrator to enable sideloading custom apps.
claims.quote: To build agents with Agents Toolkit and other IDEs, you must have your admin enable the ability to sideload a custom app to your tenant.

claims.claim: The sideloading setting is Teams admin center > Teams apps > Setup policies > Global (Org-wide default) > Upload custom apps.
claims.quote: To enable sideloading, from Teams admin center, select Teams apps > Setup policies > Global (Org-wide default), and switch the Upload custom apps toggle to On.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: An agent can be blocked at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block.
claims.quote:
Select Agents > All agents.
In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents.
In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock.

claims.claim: Blocking restricts access to the selected agent across the organisation.
claims.quote: Block and unblock | Restrict access to an agent across the organization, preventing any user from using it.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package.
claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Tenant-wide agent and plugin user access is configured at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Settings > User access to manage your organization's agents and plugins.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: All users is the default User access option.
claims.quote: All users - This option is the default. It means that all users in the organization can access agents and plugins, subject to the existing app policies and user assignments.

claims.claim: No users is an available User access option.
claims.quote: No users - This option means that no users in the organization can access agents and plugins.

claims.claim: User access can be limited to specific users or groups.
claims.quote: Specific users or groups - This option lets you select specific users or groups in your organization to have access to agents and plugins.

claims.where: controls[1].api and note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: No supported automation for this User access setting in GCC High or DoD was found; documented TCM automation is global-only.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph Copilot user access agents plugins GCC High DoD automation PowerShell userAssignmentCategory; "Copilot" "User access" "PowerShell" agents. Read agent settings, TCM agent resources and remediation/applyOnce resources; only global-service TCM automation found.

claims.claim: Learn documents preview TCM automation for microsoft.agent.useraccess.
claims.quote: This article lists the Agent resource types supported in preview for monitoring and snapshots through the Tenant Configuration Management (TCM) APIs in Microsoft Graph beta. These resources also support remediation and applyOnce.

claims.claim: The TCM useraccess resource uses properties.valueObject.userAssignmentCategory with everyone or noOne.
TCM is available only in the global service, not in national clouds.
claims.quote: TCM is available only in the global service, not in national clouds.

claims.claim: An agent lifecycle action should not be assumed to apply to its whole containing plugin package.
claims.quote: These actions apply to the selected agent. If the agent is included in a plugin, don't assume the action also applies to the whole plugin package, its skills, shared MCP servers, or connections.

claims.claim: Plugins, skills and MCP servers are managed under Agents > Tools.
claims.quote: To manage plugins, skills, and MCP servers, use Agents > Tools.

claims.claim: The pages read do not establish full availability of the Agents admin pages in GCC High or DoD, although GCCH organisation publishing is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Agents" "Settings" "User access" "GCC High". Read agent-settings and agent-actions; neither confirms the complete Agents UI for both clouds. Agent-actions says GCCH and GCCM environments support publishing agents to the organization.

claims.claim: Confirmation-prompt overrides are documented as developer configuration, with no administrator setting found.
claims.quote: Searched: "confirmation" "admin" "x-openai-isConsequential" policy; declarative agents actions GCC High DoD default enabled admin confirmation prompt policy. Read plugin-confirmation-prompts, agent-settings and policy-template excerpts; no administrator confirmation override found.
